question: How long can FD003-A100 keep flying and what is wrong with it?

documents.heading: Fan blades: inspection and blend limits

claims.text: Remaining useful life is about 27 cycles (10th-90th percentile 20-125) by the ML model; the health-index trend gives 10.
Most likely fault mode: Fan degradation (probability 1.00).
Sensors pulling the RUL estimate down most: Nc (hpc), NRc (hpc), htBleed (hpc).

Applicable documents, highest precedence first: SB-TF-72-0157 3.B, SB-TF-72-0157 1.A, AMM-TF-R3 72-21-00, AMM-TF-R3 05-20-00.
Sensors that distinguish Fan degradation from the other candidate are P30, phi, BPR, W31, W32 (not the SHAP drivers, which move under both modes).

gaps: RUL B lower bound of 3 cycles is not evidenced: EV-PRG-02 reports RUL B point estimate 10 cycles with lower 3 and upper 15, but the evidence does not show the derivation or confidence interval for the lower bound of 3 cycles. The planning lower bound calculation in EV-MNT-04 and EV-MNT-09 uses min(A 10th percentile 20, B lower 3) = 3 cycles, yet the source of the B lower value is not documented in the cited evidence items.

Part shortage rationale for engine swap not fully substantiated: The brief claims the removed engine waits for parts (TF-FAN-2101) while the lease engine is swapped in. However, EV-MNT-01 and EV-MNT-06 show FM-FAN-03 (severe on-wing replace) lists TF-FAN-2101 as short, while FM-FAN-04 (engine_change) has no parts-short annotation. EV-MNT-03 and EV-MNT-08 show TF-FAN-2101 has 0 available (75-day lead) but TF-FAN-2103 has 2 available (28-day lead). No evidence establishes that fan_degradation repair definitively requires the unavailable TF-FAN-2101 rather than the available TF-FAN-2103, leaving the engine-swap-plus-parts-wait rationale unsubstantiated versus a 28-day on-wing repair under FM-FAN-03.

dropped_notes: repeats the missing mandate challenge code refuted: Mandatory document actions missing from plan: EV-MNT-07 lists mandatory document actions for fan_degradation: AMM-TF-R3 71-00-00→FM-HPC-06, AMM-TF-R3 72-21-00→FM-FAN-01, SB-TF-72-0157 3.B→FM-FAN-01. The plan uses FM-FAN-04 and FM-FAN-03 but does not include FM-FAN-01 (inspect) or FM-HPC-06, which are linked to mandatory documents. Per precedence rules, mandatory document actions stay in the plan even next to an engine swap; their absence is a gap.

agents.name: intake
agents.role: Reads the question and resolves the engine, or asks back

agents.name: planner
agents.role: Assigns round 1, delegates follow-ups the findings call for, routes each gap to the agent that can fix it

agents.name: data
agents.role: Telemetry, input plausibility, history, schedule, slots, entered inspection findings; inspection history and targeted re-queries

agents.name: prognostics
agents.role: RUL methods A and B, SHAP drivers, anomaly flag; back-test at the last inspection

agents.name: diagnostics
agents.role: Fault-mode match and similar past cases; checks both candidates when unclear; checks an inspection finding against the fault mode

agents.name: knowledge
agents.role: Applicable documents in precedence order, mandates decided in code; the limit section for each inspection finding, compared in code; binds a missing mandate

agents.name: maint_planner
agents.role: Task, parts, slot and deadline from the RUL lower bound; applies the routed fixes

agents.name: rule_checks
agents.role: Deterministic gate: citations, numbers, parts, slots, deadlines, mandates

agents.name: critic
agents.role: Deterministic checks, then Nemotron challenges that code confirms or refutes

agents.name: escalation
agents.role: Deterministic escalation rules from the asset pack
